question: Where does the constant mean|off-diagonal cosine| between class prototypes come from, and does removing it raise the egress ceiling?
hypothesis_H_C: Every wave sums the phrase n-gram features. TEMPLATE words (the, report, read, file, ...) appear in EVERY sample regardless of the target word, so their contribution is a COMMON MODE shared across the corpus. Class prototypes therefore share a component that carries no class information but inflates every pairwise cosine.
method: Measure class-prototype crosstalk before and after subtracting the corpus mean (fit on TRAIN ONLY), then re-run held-out nearest-centroid classification. Centering is not permitted to help by leaking.

pre_registered_gates.G-C2_no_leak: mean fit on TRAIN ONLY; held-out rows never touched
pre_registered_gates.G-C4_control: content-destroyed (per-sample BLOCK permutation) control < 3x chance BOTH before and after

V8_smoke_ceiling_NOT_a_result.note: Baseline already 1.0000, so G-C3 could not discriminate. D46 lesson: the discriminating scale is where the baseline sits BELOW ceiling.

two_part_answer.part_1_hypothesis_CONFIRMED: The crosstalk is dominated by a shared template common mode. Subtracting the train-only corpus mean cuts mean|offdiag| by 10-11x (0.2086->0.0209, 0.2049->0.0186) while the content-destroyed control stays at chance and no held-out row touches the mean fit.
two_part_answer.part_2_implication_REFUTED: Removing the common mode does NOT raise the ceiling. Accuracy moves SLIGHTLY DOWN at both scales (-0.0068, -0.0044), within the G-C3 tolerance but not upward. The ~0.20 crosstalk was therefore NOT the binding constraint on classification accuracy. My own implied follow-on hypothesis is refuted by my own instrument.
two_part_answer.discriminating_signature: Within-word template crosstalk is UNCHANGED by centering (0.1401->0.1469, 0.1389->0.1458). A common mode inflates pairs of DIFFERENT classes equally and leaves class-specific structure intact. This is the exact signature of a shared component, and it is why centering removes across-class similarity without helping the decision.

bearing_on_prior_findings.crosstalk_constant_discrepancy: This corpus measures ~0.205 at V>=128; the earlier V-sweep reported ~0.343. DIFFERENT TEMPLATE FAMILIES. Both are flat in V at their own scale. The constant is family-dependent, which is itself consistent with the common-mode account (more shared template words -> larger shared component). Not a contradiction; two different corpora.
bearing_on_prior_findings.ingredient_count_law: Unaffected. That law (atomic ingredient count sets the ceiling, not manifold size) was measured on a different probe and remains standing.
bearing_on_prior_findings.what_this_does_NOT_show: It does not show the egress ceiling is irreducible. It shows this particular bias is removable AND irrelevant to accuracy, so the ceiling must lie elsewhere.

defects_found.D49: centroid_acc ended '.eq(yte)' -- a torch Tensor method on numpy arrays; would have raised AttributeError on the first call. Caught by reading back before the first run. Fixed to '=='.
defects_found.D50: wave_features returns [D/2, 2] per sample, not flat [2D], so Xtr arrived as [N, 32768, 2] and prototypes() made 3-D [K, 32768, 2]; S = P @ P.T died with 'matmul: size 32768 is different from 2'. uflat() already existed in the file for exactly this. Flatten once at collection.
defects_found.D51: At V=128 classes 64..127 had ZERO train rows (WORDS held only 64 entries) -> 'Mean of empty slice' -> nan crosstalk, nan accuracy, and the gate evaluated `nan <= nan` -> False -> printed the definite-sounding verdict CROSSTALK_NOT_COMMON_MODE from garbage. Fixed three ways: pad the vocabulary to V, derive K from the ACTUAL vocabulary, fail closed on an under-populated class, and refuse to evaluate any gate on a non-finite measurement.
defects_found.D52: My own log filter 'grep -vE "^  "' stripped every indented output line, producing a log of headers only. Rerun raw. A filter that can silently delete the data under test is itself an instrument.
